text:
jamie: quick follow-up from today's all-hands Q&A — wanted a tight summary and clear next steps on positioning.

alex: TL;DR for external: lead with customer problem (surprising inference costs + ops complexity). then our three pillars: predictable economics, unified runtime, production controls. keep it <20s.

maria: suggested 15s line: "Redwood makes LLM inference predictable: consistent latency, transparent unit costs, and an easy path from hosted to private deployments."

lee: for eng-facing docs add a short optional tech snippet: "GPU-optimized runtime, continuous batching, KV caching, and quant-friendly execution."

sam: benchmark standardization request: p50 (chat), p99 (tail), and $/1M tokens. ops-bot: please pin canonical bench.

ops-bot: canonical bench: https://redwood.internal/bench/2025-q4 (internal access)

taylor: sales note: customers ask if weare "just another endpoint". reply: start on Hosted, scale to Dedicated/Private for predictable throughput, lower unit costs, and compliance. emphasize migration path.

jamie: public competitor framing — use categories (cloud-managed, hyperscalers, self-hosted). name names only in RFPs or when we can show data.

rebecca: comms ask: can we get a single canonical paragraph for slide decks? i'll lock decks after alex shares.

alex: i'll draft the canonical paragraph after syncing with GTM Monday; avoid public numeric claims unless they link to the canonical bench.

maria: action: i'll add a short migration doc + FAQ to product docs (Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private) and open PR by Friday.

lee: i'll prepare the engineer one-pager with decision heuristics (traffic, compliance, cost targets) and example autoscale config. DM me for perf notebooks.

taylor: i'll collect top 5 sales objections and share with alex/maria.

jamie: recap: alex canonical para, maria migration doc + FAQ, lee eng one-pager, taylor objection list. thanks team. drop any follow-ups here.
